habitat: The lower layer of coastal and montane evergreen forest.
summary: A common resident. An entirely grey head, greenish upperparts and orange-yellow underparts. White stars before the eyes and on the central breast show only when the bird is excited or alarmed. Avibase marks it rare, so the months are left unset. The Kemp name Starred Robin and the code NB were left unchanged.

head.pattern: Entirely grey head. White stars before the eyes show when the bird is alarmed.

underparts.pattern: Orange-yellow underparts. A white star on the central breast shows when the bird is alarmed.

viewNotes.note: Grey head and orange-yellow underparts. The white stars show when the bird is alarmed.

calls.description: On the coast a piping too-twee. In montane areas a repeated pee, du-du WHEEE. No South African grade A recording was found. The grade A call is from Mount Kenya. The filename is XC527275-200208_04_WhiteStarredRobin.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident. Avibase marks it rare, so the months are left unset. Greenish and orange-yellow are not colour names, so only the grey head is described in prose and no upperpart or underpart colour is stored. No Kruger photograph was found. The grade A call is from Kenya. The Kemp name Starred Robin and the code NB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^6=64 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 32–128.
